newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe says no reason to change policies.
newsitem.headline: Juppe says no reason to change policies.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said on Tuesday there was no reason to change government policies in the parliamentary campaign launched on Monday.

"The president was elected in 1995," he said in an interview on France 2. "He set a course, gave a direction, he's not doing zigzags or slaloms. We are not, all of a sudden, going to change direction," he said.
"It is not about changing direction or adopting a policy contrary to what has gone before," he said.

Juppe earlier presented his campaign platform for an early parliamentary election, stressing continuation of current policies rather than radical change, while seeking to unite all wings of the centre-right coalition behind him.
He pledged to roll back the state and press ahead with and tax and spending cuts, but ruled out a shift to "the simplistic hyperliberalism of the 1980."
Juppe also reaffirmed France's commitment to launching a single European currency on time in 1999.
